components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Full-width primary action button. Solid, direct, no ambiguity.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: block; width: 100%; padding: 13px 16px; background: #2660a4; color: #edf7f6; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; border: none; border-radius: 8px; cursor: pointer; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; transition: background 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #1e4f8a; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2660a4; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary choice alongside a primary button. Transparent, bordered.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: block; width: 100%; padding: 12px 16px; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.75); color: #2660a4; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; border: 1px solid rgba(38,96,164,0.3); border-radius: 8px; cursor: pointer; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; transition: background 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: rgba(38,96,164,0.06); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2660a4; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Destructive action (leave/delete league). Explicit but calm — not alarming until tapped.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { display: block; width: 100%; padding: 11px 16px; background: transparent; color: #a32d2d; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; border: 1px solid #a32d2d; border-radius: 8px; cursor: pointer; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; transition: background 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: #fcebeb; } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #a32d2d; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
BiliBall's design language comes from a specific physical object: the framed scoreboard on the wall of a real pool hall. Legible at a glance. Bold enough to hold across a dim room. Unambiguous about who's winning. Every screen is built around this premise — the data is the decoration, and rankings are the emotional core, not an afterthought.

The palette runs two channels: a cool Competition Blue for structure and authority (nav, primary buttons, the leader's row), and a warm Amber-to-Brown register for texture and secondary hierarchy (rank labels, section cues, body copy). The page background is a faint green-tinted mist — a nod to the felt without being literal about it.

This system is RTL-native, Hebrew-first. Spatial hierarchy, reading flow, and all component layouts are built right-to-left.
keyCharacteristics: Bold ranked lists are the primary emotional surface
Two-temperature palette: cool blue authority + warm amber texture
Flat-by-default elevation; borders and background tints create separation
Light and dark modes are equal citizens
RTL layout native; LTR never assumed

rules.name: The Two-Temperature Rule
rules.body: Every screen balances cool (blue, indigo) against warm (amber, brown). Never all cool (clinical), never all warm (muddy). Tournament Blue sets the structure; Match Amber finds the details.

rules.name: The Break-White Rule
rules.body: Text on Tournament Blue is always #edf7f6, never #ffffff. Pure white on this blue reads as an oversight. The 0.5% seafoam tint is the intention.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Section labels must not use text-transform: uppercase + wide letter-spacing as a recurring scaffold. Replace with a simple color shift (Match Amber at body weight) or omit entirely when the content is self-labeling.

rules.name: The RTL-Native Rule
rules.body: All typography, spacing, and layout decisions are authored right-to-left first. direction: rtl is set at body level and inherited. No LTR overrides unless a specific Latin-script element requires it.

rules.name: The One Shadow Exception
rules.body: The pending-games banner earns a real shadow (0 2px 8px rgba(38,96,164,0.25)) because it is an interruption — a notification demanding attention. It must float above the content stream. No other surface gets a shadow at rest.

rules.name: The Inset-Only Rule
rules.body: The billiard ball avatars use inset shadows to simulate a 3D sphere. These are decorative, not structural, and belong to that specific component only. Do not apply inset shadows to cards, buttons, or inputs.

dos: Do make the leaderboard the boldest surface on the screen. Rankings carry emotional weight; they deserve visual weight.
Do use Tournament Blue for structural authority: nav, primary actions, the leader's row.
Do use Match Amber for secondary hierarchy: labels, rank numbers, timestamps.
Do write RTL-native: design all spacing, icon placement, and text alignment for right-to-left from the start.
Do keep the Felt Mist page background (#e8f5ee). It creates pool-table-adjacent warmth without being a theme park.
Do treat Break White (#edf7f6) as the only text color on Tournament Blue.
Do size the 'Add Game' bottom nav tab wider than its siblings — the primary action must command the bar.
donts: Don't use ring charts, progress streaks, or motivational banners. BiliBall is not a fitness app. This is rivalry and bragging rights, not self-improvement.
Don't apply text-transform: uppercase with wide letter-spacing to every section header. That pattern is AI-generated scaffolding, not voice.
Don't add motivational copy ('Keep pushing!', 'Great streak!'). The data speaks. Let it.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text) anywhere. Decorative, never meaningful.
Don't use thick colored side-stripe borders (border-left or border-right > 1px as an accent on cards or list items).
Don't use shadow on more than one surface at rest. The pending-games banner is the one exception.
Don't apply Celadon (#a8c69f) in light mode. It belongs to the dark mode palette only.
Don't treat the billiard ball avatar inset shadows as a general design pattern.
